#5373. OpenAI rolls out GPT-6.2 Astra for professional work and GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday work

OpenAI Group PBC today announced the launch of GPT-6.2 Astra, a new frontier artificial intelligence model for complex professional work that is claimed to outperform its predecessor at less than a third of the cost, along with an updated version of its everyday model, GPT-6.2 Sol.

The new models are aimed at businesses and developers looking for frontier performance at a cost that works at scale, with both said to deliver better results on demanding tasks while using fewer output tokens.

According to OpenAI, GPT-6.2 Astra sets a new high on Agents’ Last Exam, a benchmark that tests multistep professional work, scoring 5.2 points higher than GPT-6 Astra while costing under a third as much. It is claimed to have finished 5.5 points ahead of Anthropic PBC’s Claude Fable 5.2 at just 5% of the cost.

OpenAI is positioning GPT-6.2 Astra as the best model in the world for scientists, with the model scoring 9 percentage points higher than GPT-6 Astra on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, a benchmark for scientific work carried out in a terminal. On Harvey LAB-AA, a test of legal assignments, the model more than doubled the pass rate of Fable 5.2 at about one-sixth of the cost.

Along with improved benchmark scores, GPT-6.2 Astra was trained to create slides, spreadsheets and documents that more closely follow the conventions used by professionals in fields such as law, sales, finance and accounting. The model can match a slide template from an original file or a screenshot, including layout, colors and typography down to the exact font size.

Early testers of the model include accounting AI startup Basis, which said that its average time for long-horizon accounting work fell by 50%, with the time for its most complex work falling by up to 73%.

Described by OpenAI as its go-to model for everyday work, GPT-6.2 Sol is claimed to let users complete more tasks on the same paid plan than GPT-6.1 Sol did. According to OpenAI, the model came within 0.5 points of GPT-6.2 Astra on Cognition AI Inc.’s FrontierCode 2.0 coding benchmark at about one-fifth of the cost.

GPT-6.2 Astra comes less than two months after OpenAI called off the planned October release of GPT-6.1 Astra, after internal testing found the model fell short on staying within scope and authorization. The decision was announced the day before the company’s DevDay event in September, where GPT-6.1 Sol launched on its own.

Like GPT-6 Astra, both GPT-6.2 models meet the Critical threshold for cybersecurity under OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework, and their increased capabilities have led the company to launch them with tighter safeguards for higher-risk cybersecurity assistance that are also said to restrict some legitimate vulnerability research. The company said it will work to bring the GPT-6.2 models to Daybreak, its program for vetted cyber defenders.

GPT-6.2 Astra is also the first externally released OpenAI model to meet the High threshold for AI self-improvement, a measure of a model’s ability to accelerate AI research. OpenAI tracks the capability because models that help build future AI systems could outpace safeguards and human oversight, and earlier this month it disclosed Control Room, a system already deployed across its research infrastructure that can halt model output when intervention is needed.

The company noted that in two of its alignment tests, the new models were more likely than GPT-6 Astra to omit mentioning obstacles that blocked their work, such as a missing file. OpenAI said it has added instructions in Codex that substantially reduce the omissions and is continuing to investigate the behavior.

GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are available starting today to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex, with Enterprise and Edu access requiring a workspace admin to enable it. Developers can also access both models through the OpenAI API. API pricing for GPT-6.2 Astra is $8 per million input tokens, 40 cents for cached input and $40 per million output tokens, a 20% discount on input and output tokens compared with GPT-6 Astra. GPT-6.2 Sol carries forward GPT-6.1 Sol’s rates of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.

#5372. VeriSilicon Introduces Low-Power, High-Performance Wearable Subsystem Solution for Next-Generation AI/AR Glasses

FLEXAâ¢ Subsystem Architecture and DECNanoâ¢ Compression Technology Enable Efficient Computing, Data Transfer, and Memory Bandwidth Optimization

SHANGHAI, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- VeriSilicon (688521.SH) announced its low-power, high-performance wearable subsystem solution for next-generation AI and augmented reality (AR) glasses. Building on its experience in the wearable market, VeriSilicon combines its broad portfolio of low-power processing IPs, including the new glasses-focused Nano-XR series, with subsystem-level architecture optimization to deliver power-efficient solutions for a wide range of glasses applications. The solution integrates a range of processing capabilities, including image and video processing, AI computing, voice and audio processing, display processing, and graphics rendering, enabling flexible and efficient system designs.

The new glasses-focused Nano-XR series extends VeriSilicon's established low-power Nano IP portfolio to address the specific requirements of AI/AR glasses. ISPNanoUltra-XR delivers smartphone-level photo and video quality with optimized power consumption and silicon area, while ISPPico-XR is designed for IR sensor applications, supporting always-on functions such as eye tracking and gesture recognition. DCNanoUltra-XR provides low-latency display processing for 3DoF/6DoF applications, featuring power-gating strategies and support for multiple high-speed display interfaces. GCNanoOptimaV-XR builds upon the widely adopted GCNanoUltraV, offering enhanced projection transformation capabilities, higher graphics performance, and a reduced memory footprint for glasses applications.

Beyond the Nano-XR series, VeriSilicon offers a comprehensive portfolio of processing IPs spanning Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) IP, Neural Network Processing Unit (NPU) IP, Video Processing Unit (VPU) IP, Digital Signal Processing (DSP) IP, Image Signal Processing (ISP) IP and Display Processing IP, with configurable options to address different power and performance requirements. Its DSP IPs support voice processing, noise reduction, audio codecs, and Cat.1/Cat.4-related applications in wearable devices, while its NPU IPs support diverse AI workloads, including low-power wake-up, image enhancement, and general-purpose AI computing. Customers can select and configure different IPs according to their specific application scenarios and computing requirements, enabling solutions ranging from basic, low-power glasses to advanced AR devices with richer computing and display capabilities. Support for RTOS, Linux, and Android further accommodates diverse application requirements.

At the subsystem level, VeriSilicon optimizes the overall processing architecture by enabling efficient data flows across different processing blocks and minimizing unnecessary data transfers and external memory accesses. Its DECNano compression technology enables visually lossless compression, reducing external PSRAM and DDR capacity and bandwidth requirements. Meanwhile, the FLEXA interface communication technology supports segment-level data exchange between processing IPs, using on-chip SRAM to buffer intermediate data and further reduce external memory accesses and end-to-end latency.

"Smart glasses are rapidly evolving to support increasingly sophisticated applications that integrate sensing, image capture, AI processing, and advanced display capabilities. Delivering these experiences requires not only power-efficient individual IPs, but also seamless integration and optimized collaboration across the entire subsystem," said Weijin Dai, Chief Strategy Officer, Executive Vice President and General Manager of the IP Division at VeriSilicon. "Building on our proven success in the wearable market with our comprehensive Nano IP portfolio, spanning camera, AI processing, graphics, and display technologies, we are taking the next step by introducing our Nano-XR IP series and integrated wearable subsystem solution. By leveraging our FLEXA subsystem architecture and DECNano compression technology, we enable efficient collaboration among IP building blocks, significantly improving data movement efficiency while reducing memory bandwidth requirements, processing latency, and power consumption. We are also actively collaborating with customers on dedicated smart glasses chip designs incorporating Nano-XR IPs to enable more advanced AI/AR applications and next-generation wearable experiences."

VeriSilicon Microelectronics (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. (VeriSilicon, 688521.SH) is a leading publicly listed provider of custom silicon solutions, with a comprehensive and proprietary portfolio of semiconductor IPs, and a long-standing focus on AI ASIC custom silicon. For more information, please visit: www.verisilicon.com

#5371. Fitch warns of growing balance-sheet strain at top nonbank mortgage firms

Fitch Ratings affirmed long-term issuer default ratings for nine nonbank mortgage lenders but revised outlooks on Pennymac, Planet and Freedom to negative, citing elevated leverage, concentrated MSR exposure and profitability constraints expected in 2027.   AI Summary

Fitch Ratings revised its outlooks on three major nonbank mortgage companies to negative and warned that elevated leverage and growing mortgage servicing rights (MSR) exposure are weighing on credit profiles in a higher-for-longer rate environment.

In a periodic review of nine publicly rated nonbank mortgage firms released Monday, Fitch affirmed all long-term issuer default ratings but shifted the outlooks for Pennymac Financial Services, Planet Financial Group and Freedom Mortgage Holdings to negative from stable.

Fitch maintained the following long-term issuer default ratings: Onity Group at B-, UWM Holdings Corp. at B+, Pennymac at BB, Planet at B, CrossCountry Mortgage at BB-, Rocket Companies at BBB-, Freedom at BB-, Finance of America at CCC and Provident Funding Associates at B.

Fitch said profitability for several lenders is likely to be constrained in 2027, given a challenging rate backdrop that limits refinance volume and makes it harder for companies to retain earnings and pay down debt. That dynamic is expected to pressure leverage ratios across the sector.

At Pennymac, corporate leverage has exceeded Fitch’s 1.5x downgrade trigger since the first quarter of 2026. And a failure to make meaningful progress toward reducing corporate leverage to 1.5x or less over the outlook horizon could lead to a downgrade to BB-, Fitch said.

“Fitch expects profitability to be constrained in 2027 by a challenging rate environment and the lag in realizing the full impact of recent expense reduction initiatives,” Fitch stated.

For Planet, the agency pointed to a significant increase in MSR exposure since 2021, as the company retained servicing from its own originations and acquired bulk portfolios. MSRs represented about 363% of company equity in the second quarter of 2026, up from 293% a year earlier and above the level of higher-rated peers, Fitch said.

Planet’s corporate leverage also rose to 5.5x, up from 4.3x during the same period. Fitch considers that level high and a key constraint on the rating. The agency said it could downgrade Planet if leverage rises above its 7.0x trigger.

At Freedom, corporate leverage — measured as gross nonfunding debt to tangible equity — reached Fitch’s 2.0x downgrade trigger in the second quarter, up from 1.9x at the end of 2025. Shareholder distributions exceeded earnings in the first half of the year, contributing to the increase.

Fitch expects Freedom’s leverage to rise further as it grows its servicing portfolio and uses available borrowing capacity to meet potential margin calls under its hedging program.

At UWM, Fitch cited high leverage, MSR valuation risk and reliance on short-term, largely uncommitted secured funding as constraints on its rating. Corporate leverage, excluding origination funding, climbed to 5.3x in the third quarter of 2026, nearly double the 2.7x figure at the end of 2025.

MSR mark-to-market volatility and a $603 million hedge loss in the second quarter have weighed on profitability. Still, Fitch pointed to a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin for the trailing 12 months through the third quarter as evidence of solid core earnings.

“Fitch expects leverage to decline over time, supported by planned MSR sales and earnings above the expected $165 million annual preferred dividend. Common dividends are suspended. Even so, Fitch expects corporate leverage to remain above 2.0x over the Outlook horizon.”

Regarding CCM, its acquisition of Two Harbors Investment Corp. brought $156 billion in unpaid principal balance to its servicing portfolio, along with the RoundPoint Mortgage Servicing platform’s in-house capabilities. Fitch expects the added scale and greater retention of servicing economics to improve profitability, although it does not anticipate the full integration benefits until the end of 2028.

The acquisitions also drove up leverage. Corporate leverage rose to 2.9x, up from 1.2x and above Fitch’s 2.0x rating sensitivity. Fitch expects CCM to reduce leverage toward its 1.0x corporate target. Failure to bring leverage below downgrade triggers within 12 to 24 months could result in a negative rating action.

At Rocket, corporate leverage stood at 1.1x in the third quarter, down from 1.4x at the end of 2025 but above the 0.5x recorded at the end of 2024, before its acquisitions of Redfin and Mr. Cooper Group.

Although Rocket remains above Fitch’s 1.0x downgrade trigger, the agency expects leverage to fall below that level over the next 12 months through repayment of secured borrowings and moderate earnings retention. The pace will depend on market conditions and whether the company realizes the expected acquisition synergies, Fitch said.

#5369. Strategy Bitcoin vs. BitMine Ethereum: Which Crypto Treasury Is Better Positioned for a Market Recovery?

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Strategy is buying more Bitcoin while Tom Lee’s BitMine keeps loading up on Ethereum. Both companies are doubling down as crypto prices slide. But their latest purchases reveal two very different bets on the next bull market. Strategy added another 485 BTC, taking its treasury to 850,849 Bitcoin. Meanwhile, BitMine’s Ethereum holdings have climbed to more than 6.07 million ETH, worth $11 billion at current prices.

Neither company is backing away. In fact, both are positioning themselves for a recovery that could dramatically revalue their massive crypto treasuries. The question is which strategy has the better chance of delivering the biggest payoff.

Michael Saylor’s Strategy acquired 485 BTC for $33.4 million between November 9 and November 15, according to its latest SEC filing. The company paid an average of $68,887 per coin, bringing its total holdings to 850,849 BTC.

Strategy has acquired 485 $BTC and repurchased $228M of $STRC. As of 11/15/26, we hold 850,849 BTC and $4.9B of USD Assets. $MSTR https://t.co/cACnaFSMsr

Strategy has now spent $64.2 billion accumulating Bitcoin, with an average acquisition price of $75,452. At Bitcoin’s recent price near $64,200, the treasury is worth roughly $54.6 billion, leaving the company with an estimated $9.6 billion unrealized loss.

That is a substantial paper loss, but Saylor’s accumulation strategy has never depended on buying every Bitcoin at the bottom. Strategy continues using capital markets to expand its position, betting that Bitcoin’s long-term appreciation will eventually overwhelm short-term volatility.

Its latest filing also revealed $244.7 million in proceeds from common stock sales. Strategy allocated $33.4 million toward Bitcoin purchases, while spending $228.1 million repurchasing its STRC preferred shares.

That second transaction is worth watching. Strategy is managing its capital structure while maintaining its Bitcoin accumulation machine. It also reported $4.75 billion in its USD Reserve. The company already controls more than 850,000 BTC, giving shareholders enormous exposure to Bitcoin’s next major move.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

Tom Lee is playing a different game. BitMine’s Ethereum holdings reached 6,070,092 ETH following its latest disclosed purchase of 9,587 ETH. The position represents 4.97% of Ethereum’s circulating supply, bringing the company within touching distance of its ambitious 5% accumulation target.

🧵1/BitMine provided its latest holdings update for November 16, 2026$11.8 billion in total crypto + "moonshots":– 6,077,745 ETH at $1,823 per ETH (per @coinbase)– 216 Bitcoin (BTC)– $180 million stake in Beast Industries @MrBeast– $67 million stake in Eightco Holdings…

At recent prices around $1,820, those holdings are worth $11 billion. But BitMine has another advantage that Strategy cannot replicate with its Bitcoin treasury: staking income.

The company has already staked 5.23 million ETH, or more than 86% of its holdings. Tom Lee projected that fully staking its Ethereum treasury could generate approximately $359 million in annualized rewards.

That creates a potentially powerful combination. BitMine is accumulating a substantial share of Ethereum’s supply while putting most of its holdings to work.

Lee’s thesis extends beyond ETH price appreciation. He sees Ethereum benefiting from institutional tokenization, financial infrastructure moving onchain, and growing demand for blockchain-based settlement.

If those trends accelerate, BitMine could benefit from both Ethereum appreciation and recurring staking rewards.

This is where the competition gets interesting. Strategy has the larger dollar-denominated crypto treasury, but BitMine has a compelling argument for capital efficiency. Bitcoin offers a straightforward scarcity thesis, while Ethereum adds staking and exposure to expanding blockchain activity.

Strategy’s biggest advantage is its enormous Bitcoin position. With 850,849 BTC, even a substantial recovery in Bitcoin could translate into billions of dollars in additional treasury value.

BitMine, however, has built an Ethereum position approaching 5% of circulating supply. Its staking operation gives the company another potential source of returns while waiting for the next market expansion.

There is also a difference in what investors are buying. Strategy offers a concentrated Bitcoin treasury vehicle, while BitMine offers a leveraged corporate bet on Ethereum’s future financial infrastructure.

Our verdict? BitMine has the more productive treasury model, but Strategy remains the heavyweight in corporate crypto accumulation.

If Bitcoin leads the next recovery, Saylor could quickly reclaim the spotlight. If Ethereum outperforms and institutional adoption accelerates, Lee’s strategy could look considerably smarter.

Both companies are effectively making the same bet: today’s market weakness will look insignificant when the next major crypto cycle arrives.

The winner may ultimately depend on which asset leads that recovery. But neither Saylor nor Lee appears interested in waiting for confirmation before accumulating.

#5368. Token sticker shock pushes enterprises from frontier labs toward open-weight AI factories

Enterprises have spent the AI boom racing to secure GPUs, but the harder decisions now sit above the hardware. Token bills, data sovereignty and model choice increasingly decide which AI pilots reach production, a shift on display at the SC26 supercomputing conference.

Dell Technologies Inc. has spent the past year pushing its AI Factory beyond servers and storage. Customers now want a full-stack outcome that covers software, open-source tools, models and operations, according to Brad Maltz (pictured), senior director of AI solutions at Dell.

“The hardware’s key, because that drives the tokens,” Maltz said. “You really, truly need a full-stack AI factory view above and beyond just the hardware stack.”

Maltz spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how token bills and data sovereignty are steering enterprises toward open-weight models and a full-stack AI Factory. The interview came as Dell rolled out AI Factory updates at the conference. (* Disclosure below.)

Many enterprises are still stuck in pilot mode, and coding assistants are often the easiest place to start. Employees have already tried tools from Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC, so teams want to apply that experience to business use cases. Once those pilots grow, the bill arrives, Maltz explained.

“The token spend right now in the frontier labs and the hyperscalers. That’s a little more than we expected,” Maltz said. “We didn’t expect to spend $10,000, $20,000 per person per month.”

Cost is only one trigger. Data sovereignty, intellectual property leakage, security and governance all have to be addressed before a pilot goes live. That is steering many enterprises toward open-weight models they can fine-tune and run on-premises, including U.S. options such as Nvidia Corp.’s Nemotron, according to Maltz.

“There will always be frontier labs. There will always be open-weight models,” Maltz said. “The question is going to be, do we have enough diversity with the open weights to meet the enterprise use cases?”

To keep pace, Dell launched its AI Ecosystem Program to validate software partners on its AI Factory. About 60 more partners have applied or are under evaluation, and each addition lets Dell solve 10 to 30 more customer problems, Maltz noted. For sovereign deployments, that often means disconnected, on-premises systems that keep models next to the GPUs and data enterprises already control.

“People understand data is the lifeblood of AI,” Maltz said. “It’s the thing that trains the models. It’s the thing the models operate against. It comes from your enterprise business applications.”

#5367. Fitch affirms Finance of America’s CCC rating as key risks, leverage persist

Fitch Ratings affirmed Finance of America Companies' long-term issuer default rating at CCC with a positive outlook, citing improved liquidity and better underlying profitability as the company addresses near-term debt maturities. The agency maintained Finance of America Funding’s senior secured rating at CCC- with an RR5 recovery rating. Despite FOA’s leading position in reverse mortgages, Fitch highlighted weak liquidity, very high leverage of 33.7x, a largely secured and short-term funding structure, and earnings pressure from interest rate volatility.   AI Summary

Finance of America Companies’ long-term credit ratings remain deep in speculative-grade territory, even as the company reduces near-term risk and improves underlying profitability, according to a review published Monday by Fitch Ratings.

Fitch this week affirmed the long-term issuer default ratings of Finance of America Companies and its subsidiaries, Finance of America Equity Capital LLC and Finance of America Funding LLC, with a CCC rating and a positive outlook. Fitch also affirmed Finance of America Funding’s senior secured debt rating at CCC- with a recovery rating of RR5.

Fitch defines CCC ratings as having a very low margin for safety, with default considered a real possibility. But the ratings agency also explained that it maintains a positive outlook for Finance of America (FOA) due to its “established market position within the reverse mortgage sector,” along with experience senior management and support from Brian Libman, who chairs its board of directors.

The action is part of Fitch’s periodic peer review of nine publicly rated nonbank mortgage companies. Like other lenders, FOA has been contending with volatile interest rates, high leverage and constrained liquidity as the broader mortgage market remains cyclical and capital intensive.

Earlier this month, FOA reported a net loss of $110 million in the third quarter of 2026 as noncash fair value adjustments offset growth in its home equity lending business. The company reported funded loan volume of $748 million from July through September, up 24% from the same period in 2025, while its year-to-date volume of $2.07 billion was up 17% year over year.

The company also said during its Q3 earnings call that it expects to complete a $60 million paydown of senior secured notes in November. In June 2024, FOA announced a restructuring of unsecured debt into secure notes while extending the original 2025 maturity date. That debt was restructured into two tranches, with $200 million in secured first-lien notes due in 2026 (along with an option to extend to 2027) and $150 million in exchangeable senior first-lien notes due in 2029.

In its report, Fitch said the positive outlook reflects FOA’s work over the past year to address material near-term obligations and its improved profitability when excluding fair value marks.

The agency indicated it could raise FOA’s issuer default rating to B- if the company builds a “substantial” liquidity cushion beyond remaining repayment obligations and continues to de-lever through retained earnings.

The ratings remain constrained by relatively weak liquidity and high leverage, a short-term and largely secured funding profile, and elevated key person risk tied to Libman. Additionally, the review factored in the highly cyclical nature of mortgage originations, as well as the volatility tied to mortgage servicing rights valuations and securitization residuals.

The announcement illustrates that while FOA has taken steps to stabilize its balance sheet, its capital structure and earnings volatility still present elevated credit risk for mortgage and capital markets participants — including warehouse lenders and secondary market investors.

Fitch noted that its positive outlook could be revised to stable, or the CCC rating could be cut, if Finance of America fails to bolster its liquidity before upcoming maturities.

Other factors that could drive a downgrade include deteriorating profitability and sustained leverage above 15s. The ratings agency said that FOA’s ratio of total debt to tangible equity — excluding obligations tied to HECM Mortgage-Backed Securities (HMBS) and nonrecourse debt — was 33.7x at the end of September, up from 14.0x at the end of 2025. Fitch said it believes leverage will stay sensitive to interest rate movements.

In December 2025, FOA issued $50 million of preferred stock to funds managed by Blue Owl Capital. Fitch treats these preferred shares as debt, since change-of-control provisions mandate redemption of the preferred shares in cash. But the agency said it does not believe the preferred shares will be a permanent part of FOA’s capital structure as scheduled increases in coupons, starting with a 300-bps increase at the seventh anniversary date, provide an incentive to redeem and create an effective maturity.

“We think it speaks a lot to the interest in the reverse segment, the fact that they’re willing to make an equity commitment to us and acquire the product that we’re generating,” FOA CEO Graham Fleming told HousingWire‘s Reverse Mortgage Daily earlier this year about the transaction.

Fitch also noted potential upsides for FOA’s ratings. These include sustained improvement in liquidity after near-term obligations are repaid, return on average assets being maintained above 1% with positive cash generation, and gross leverage staying below 10x.

The agency also cited better funding flexibility through long-term and more committed facilities, growth that strengthens the FOA franchise brand, and deeper management expertise and clear succession planning as potential reasons to bolster the company’s ratings down the road.

#5366. ISDN Holdings Limited Receives Frost & Sullivan's 2026 Asia-Pacific Customer Value Leadership Recognition for Integrated Industrial Automation Intelligence Leadership

ISDN Holdings Limited is recognized for combining full-stack industrial automation capabilities, application-focused engineering, and customer-centric innovation to deliver measurable value across APAC.

KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Frost & Sullivan is pleased to announce that ISDN Holdings Limited (ISDN) has received the 2026 Asia-Pacific Customer Value Leadership Recognition in the integrated industrial automation intelligence industry for its strong customer-centric strategy, engineering expertise, and ability to deliver integrated automation solutions across diverse industrial environments. The recognition highlights ISDN's sustained focus on solving complex customer requirements through technology-agnostic integration, localized engineering support, and lifecycle service capabilities.

Frost & Sullivan evaluates companies through a rigorous benchmarking process across two core dimensions: business impact and customer impact. ISDN demonstrated strength across both dimensions by aligning its technology capabilities with evolving industrial requirements while executing solutions with agility across the Asia-Pacific region.

"ISDN combines deep engineering expertise and broad technology capabilities with the agility, responsiveness, and customer focus needed to solve complex automation challenges across Asia's diverse industrial landscape. This unique combination creates a differentiated market position," said Arun Prasath, Principal Consultant at Frost & Sullivan.

Founded in 1986 and headquartered in Singapore, ISDN has developed into a full-stack industrial automation company serving more than 10,000 customers through approximately 75 offices across Asia. Its capabilities span motion control, system solutions, precision manufacturing, software, and renewable energy, supporting sectors including semiconductors, Industry 4.0 manufacturing, medical devices, industrial robotics, aerospace, and clean energy.

ISDN's technology-agnostic approach and broad ecosystem of global technology partners enable it to combine components and technologies into application-specific solutions while providing localized engineering expertise. Its capabilities extend across motion control, edge-to-cloud integration, industrial connectivity, machine analytics, IIoT, cloud and edge computing, and intelligent manufacturing.

Innovation remains central to ISDN's customer value proposition. The company has expanded its capabilities up the automation stack through in-house software, AI-enabled industrial tools, and turnkey solutions. Its AI-powered industrial alarm management solution, for example, collects signals from intelligent sensors, devices, controllers, and IIoT systems, prioritizes alerts, and assigns tasks to relevant personnel through existing communication platforms. Deployments across an oil company in Thailand, a semiconductor manufacturing facility in Singapore, and a Singapore data center demonstrate its application-focused approach.

"For the past 40 years, ISDN and our subsidiaries have worked quietly behind the scenes of industrial automation, making technologies work together and keeping our customers' operations moving. This recognition brings that collective contribution into focus. Our strength lies in understanding each customer's challenges and combining engineering expertise, technology and local support to deliver practical results. As we expand into AI-enabled automation, our purpose remains the same: to improve productivity, strengthen operational reliability and help customers adapt to changing demands. We thank our customers, technology partners and teams across Asia for making this possible." - Mr. Teo Cher Koon, President, and Managing Director of ISDN Holdings Limited

ISDN's customer-first model is reinforced by its full-stack engineering capabilities and modular organizational structure. By combining in-house engineering, precision manufacturing, software development, system integration, and a regional partner ecosystem, the company can customize solutions while addressing requirements across the asset lifecycle. Its smart warehouse solution, developed with Schneider Electric, has delivered a 50% productivity gain, a 91% reduction in stocktaking time, and a 33% decrease in manpower.

"ISDN's high retention among top accounts reflects a consistent track record of application-accurate solutioning. The company engages with customers at the requirements stage to understand their needs and deliver desired outcomes. This discipline, sustained over 40 years and now extended to AI-enabled tools, underpins its customer satisfaction metrics and competitive positioning," said Iqra Azam, Best Practices Research Analyst at Frost & Sullivan.

Frost & Sullivan commends ISDN for establishing a differentiated model that combines technical depth, application-specific customization, regional responsiveness, and sustained customer engagement. Its continued expansion into high-growth areas including semiconductors, data centers, intelligent factories, energy storage, renewable energy, and physical AI further reflects its focus on evolving industrial requirements.

Each year, Frost & Sullivan presents the Customer Value Leadership Recognition to a company that demonstrates a strong ability to create measurable value for customers through effective strategy, execution, innovation, and sustained customer engagement.

Frost & Sullivan Best Practices Recognition

Frost & Sullivan's Best Practices Recognitions honor companies across regional and global markets that exhibit exceptional achievement and consistent excellence in areas such as leadership, technological innovation, customer experience, and strategic product development. Each recognition is the result of a rigorous analytical process in which Frost & Sullivan industry experts benchmark performance through comprehensive interviews, deep-dive analysis, and extensive secondary research. The goal is to identify true best-in-class organizations that are driving transformative growth and setting new industry standards.

#5365. Voltage Energy Unveils Microgrid System and New EBOS Solutions at RE+ 2026

New offerings support rapid deployment and better energy economics for mission-critical power while improving installation efficiency and project flexibility in utility-scale solar.

TIMBERLAKE, N.C., Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Voltage Energy Group ("Voltage Energy"), a leading global provider of mission-critical power architecture solutions for utility-scale solar, BESS, and data center segments,  today unveiled its Microgrid System (MGS) and introduced two new electrical balance of system (EBOS) products, the Load Break Disconnect Box (LBD) and Combiner Box (CBX), at RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas.

The new offerings highlight two areas of innovation: rapidly deployable off-grid power for mission-critical applications and an expanding EBOS portfolio for utility-scale solar projects. Together, they demonstrate Voltage Energy's engineering expertise in delivering practical, reliable power infrastructure solutions across diverse energy applications.

Rapidly Deployable Power for Mission-Critical Applications

Making its debut at RE+ 2026, Voltage Energy's Microgrid System (MGS) combines solar generation and battery storage in a modular off-grid system. It features foldable PV racking and a pre-assembled Power Skid that integrates the inverter, batteries, junction equipment, and backup diesel generators. Factory pre-wiring simplifies on-site connections, while foldable PV racking supports faster installation and redeployment. Adjustable screw-jack legs accommodate slopes and uneven terrain.

Designed for rapid deployment, a 64 kW MGS system can be installed by a three-person team in 24 hours under suitable installation conditions. An illustrative energy cost comparison also indicates approximately 40% lower energy costs than on-site diesel generation, depending on operating assumptions.

MGS supports temporary and mission-critical power needs across utility-scale solar construction, data center construction, disaster relief, and mining site. From powering construction activities to providing electricity for time-sensitive emergency operations after natural disasters, the system delivers reliable off-grid power when and where it matters most.

Expanding EBOS Solutions with New LBD and CBX

Alongside MGS, Voltage Energy introduced its new LBD and CBX, further expanding its EBOS portfolio for utility-scale solar projects. Supporting both Trunk Bus and Multi-String architectures, these products give developers and EPCs greater flexibility in selecting DC collection solutions tailored to their project layouts, electrical requirements, and installation plans.

For Trunk Bus architecture, LYNX PLUS provides a modular solution that aggregates power from multiple PV strings along a shared trunk. The new LBD adds a defined disconnect point, allowing electrical isolation of sections of the DC power system. For Multi-String architecture, IBEX PLUS and IBEX solutions group PV strings into customized harness assemblies for flexible routing across varied project layouts. The new CBX combines up to 16 PV string inputs into a single output toward the inverter, while supporting parallel output conductors and maintaining access to fuses for O&M.

Founded in North Carolina in 2016, Voltage Energy continues to expand its U.S. manufacturing footprint while building on its engineering expertise. Its Voltage Power Ranch in Timberlake, North Carolina, entered the pilot-run stage in October 2026, with a planned capacity ramp through 2027. The facility reinforces the company's commitment to engineering quality and reliable project execution for domestic energy infrastructure.

From mission-critical off-grid power to engineered EBOS solutions for utility-scale solar, Voltage Energy draws on its engineering expertise and manufacturing capabilities to meet today's project needs and support tomorrow's energy demands. Visitors can explore Voltage Energy's latest solutions at Booths N936 and N736 during RE+ 2026, November 17â19, in Las Vegas.

Voltage Energy delivers innovative, value-engineered technologies and services that improve installation efficiency, enhance safety, and optimize long-term system performance.We are a group of innovative people who sincerely care about the renewable industry. #5364. Business as usual for Nvidia as it beats expectations in first earnings call after Jensen Huang’s resignation

Nvidia Corp. delivered earnings and revenue that surpassed Wall Street’s expectations and offered strong guidance for the current quarter in its first earnings call since the shocking resignation of its iconic co-founder and Chief Executive Jensen Huang.

The results were so impressive that they slammed the brakes on a weeklong slide, as Nvidia’s stock rose more than 4% in late trading today.

The chipmaker reported third-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of $2.68 per share, surpassing Wall Street’s target of $2.48 per share by a comfortable margin. Revenue for the period came to $115.84 billion, more than double a year earlier and above the $109.1 billion consensus estimate.

The vast majority of those sales stemmed from Nvidia’s core data center business, which delivered revenue of $107.6 billion, higher than the Street’s $101.87 billion forecast. For the current quarter, Nvidia said it’s expecting its revenue to grow by about 90%, to $130 billion. Though that suggests a slowdown sequentially from the prior quarter, it’s still nicely above Wall Street’s target of $125.1 billion.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress (pictured, with Huang in the background) has become a familiar face to analysts on Nvidia’s conference calls, but today she found herself in a very different position. For the first time, she was fielding questions as the company’s interim CEO, which means her responsibilities now go well beyond the numbers. She was joined on the call by Nvidia’s Chairman of the Board Harvey Jones, who insisted that the board has no intention of bringing Huang back as CEO.

Nvidia has been under a cloud all week following the abrupt resignation of Huang, which came days after he admitted to having an affair with a businesswoman who’s alleged to be a Chinese spy. In the days that followed that scandal, which included rumors of a second affair with an Nvidia executive and also a potential third fling with yet another company employee, the chipmaker’s stock had been in a downward spiral. But that trend was finally reversed following the company’s strong guidance today.

One of the central questions investors had going into the call was if Nvidia would scrap its previous forecast for 70% revenue growth in the fiscal year ending January 2028. However, Kress did the opposite and raised the company’s full-year guidance to 75% growth.

In raising the company’s outlook, Kress told analysts on the call that “it’s business as usual at Nvidia,” despite all that has happened. And indeed, throughout much of her commentary, she focused strictly to the numbers that revealed a business still in good health. With regard to the guidance, Kress stressed that this forecast “considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of customer demand and our customers’ access to capital.”

“Our leadership has stood up so strongly over the last week to support both what we are doing here at earnings, but also supporting all of our different employees around the world,” Kress said. “Remember, we have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class, multiyear roadmap. And I think that’s important from a business perspective.”

Kress said Nvidia expects frontier labs such as OpenAI Group PBC, Anthropic Group PBC and others to account for about 15% of its data center revenue this year, in a sign that they’re increasingly standing up their own data center infrastructure rather than renting from cloud providers.

“As frontier models become more capable, adoption and revenue are scaling rapidly, with Anthropic annualized revenue reaching $181 billion at the end of October,” Kress said.

Another big chunk of Nvidia’s revenue comes from so-called neocloud infrastructure providers. Much of the money those customers spend on its chips stems from a complex web of financing, with much of it being traceable back to Nvidia itself. Kress told analysts that the company is continuing to help neoclouds and frontier labs to secure the land, power and data center capacity they need to grow, and that it may be willing to share revenue from neoclouds together with the upfront sales of its products, if they meet certain conditions.

Kress said Nvidia currently has more than $32 billion in total commitments to neoclouds through 2032, but insisted that these take effect only if those customers are able to “secure the funding they need to purchase the data center infrastructure products they require, and if the related compute capacity is deployed and made operational.”

Another closely watched number is Nvidia’s gross margin, which has narrowed in recent quarters as its supply commitments have slowly piled up. Investors will have been pleased to see that Nvidia beat Wall Street’s expectations on that metric, with its nonstandard gross margin ending the quarter at 74.9%, above the forecast of 74%. Its margins still declined compared to the previous quarter, though, blamed on the ramping up of production of its latest generation Rubin graphics processing units.

Despite the after-hours gain, Nvidia’s stock is still down 24% this month, and last Friday it completed its sixth successive weekly decline. That’s the company’s longest losing streak since 2012, and its shares are now trading at their lowest level since July 2025.

The decline began several weeks before news of Huang’s extramarital escapades became public knowledge. The company has also faced rising concerns about a possible slowdown in the artificial intelligence industry and a political shift in Washington D.C. as a result of the Republicans’ stunning losses during the midterm elections earlier this month.

Despite Jones’s insistence that Huang will not be returning to the CEO role, the prospect of his doing so cannot be ruled out. In his first public comments since his ousting, Huang said in a post on X that “if the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

There are plenty of people who would like to see Huang return, including U.S. President Donald Trump and various luminaries from the technology world. Last Thursday, someone created an online petition calling for the reinstatement of Huang, and it has been signed by names including Elon Musk, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games Inc. CEO Tim Sweeney.

It could be possible that Huang ends up returning to the company in a different capacity than CEO. Susquehanna analyst Chris Rolland told CNBC that the chipmaker could end up taking him back under a new role, such as a consultant or a strategic adviser.

“I think that helps bridge the gap here, he can give technical and strategic advisory services that I think would be incredibly important to the company,” the analyst said.

#5363. U.S. kindergarten MMR coverage sits 2.6 points below the WHO target

Free daily briefing on global business news.

These 10 points explain falling MMR vaccination rates, U.S. kindergarten coverage of 92.4% against WHO's 95% target and the reported loss of measles-free status

A few percentage points of vaccine coverage separate the level WHO recommends for measles herd immunity from where U.S. kindergartners stand today. For 26 years, the U.S. held measles-free status. This slideshow examines falling MMR vaccination rates, the pressures public health experts connect to them and what it would take to close that gap.

A Trump administration official said on Monday that the Pan American Health Organization told the administration, in a letter sent Friday, that the U.S. had lost its measles-free status. The official spoke anonymously because the decision was not yet public. PAHO was expected to announce it formally on Tuesday. Reuters reported the official's account.

The reported loss comes as the country deals with its largest number of measles cases in more than three decades. About 7,700 people have been infected and 13 have died since 2025. In August, the CDC reported kindergarten vaccination coverage of 92.4% for the 2025-26 school year. WHO recommends that 95% of people receive two doses of the MMR vaccine. The difference is 2.6 percentage points. That number describes kindergartners, not the population as a whole.

Reuters reports that the surge coincides with falling immunization rates and rising vaccine hesitancy under Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Trust in vaccination dropped during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Several experts quoted by Reuters said messaging from Kennedy and the White House about MMR risks has worsened those concerns.

The 10 slides below take up those issues one at a time. They cover the reported loss of elimination status, the kindergarten coverage figure and the 95% herd immunity target. They also examine low-vaccination pockets in individual schools, eroding public trust, federal messaging on vaccine risks and pressure on states to loosen school mandates. The final slides turn to imported cases, the Utah outbreak that figured in PAHO's review and the steps required to regain measles-free status.

The U.S. has lost the measles-free status it held for 26 years, according to a Trump administration official. The official said the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) delivered that decision to the administration in a letter.

PAHO sent the letter on Friday. The official described it to Reuters on Monday.

The official spoke on condition of anonymity because the decision had not yet been made public. PAHO was expected to announce the decision formally on Tuesday. Until that announcement, the account of the letter rests on the official's description.

The letter did more than deliver a verdict. PAHO also urged the U.S. to step up vaccination to halt the spread of the virus, according to the official.

U.S. kindergarten vaccination coverage was 92.4% for the 2025-26 school year, the CDC reported in August. That is 2.6 percentage points short of the 95% level the World Health Organization recommends.

The figure applies to one group: children entering kindergarten in the 2025-26 school year. It is not a measure of how many Americans of all ages are protected against measles.

The CDC number is a nationwide snapshot of a single school year. By itself, it does not show how coverage has changed over time.

What it does show is the distance between current kindergarten coverage and the WHO benchmark. The WHO recommendation calls for 95% of people to receive two doses of the MMR vaccine. A national kindergarten figure below that mark means fewer children starting school are covered than the benchmark calls for.

Two doses of the MMR vaccine are 97% effective at stopping measles from spreading. The World Health Organization recommends that 95% of people receive both doses to reach herd immunity.

The two figures measure different things. The 97% figure describes how well the vaccine works in a person who completes both doses. The 95% figure describes how much of a population needs that protection.

The WHO benchmark counts people who have received two doses. A single shot does not meet it.

Herd immunity is the protection that a highly vaccinated population gives to people who cannot be vaccinated themselves. Those people have no vaccine-derived protection of their own.

They depend on high vaccination among the people around them to keep the virus from reaching them.

Some individual schools in Spartanburg County, South Carolina, reported vaccination rates as low as 20% during the state's measles outbreak earlier this year. At that level, most children in those schools were not vaccinated.

A national average cannot show gaps like these. The countrywide kindergarten figure combines schools with high and low rates into a single number.

That means a national rate close to the herd immunity target can still include individual schools where coverage is a fraction of it. The Spartanburg County schools are one such case.

Walter Orenstein, a professor emeritus at Emory University, described the task in terms of reach rather than averages. "What we need to do is terminate the current transmission," he said. "To do that, we need to enhance immunization uptake in virtually all communities."

His wording sets the goal at the level of individual communities, not the country as a whole.

Public trust in vaccination dropped during the COVID-19 pandemic and kept dropping in the period after it. Josh Michaud, a public health analyst with KFF, said rebuilding that trust depends on time and on public health officials themselves.

Reuters lists this loss of trust among the pressures that coincide with falling immunization rates in the U.S. The decline it describes concerns trust in vaccination generally.

Michaud set out what recovery would require. "Regaining that trust takes time, and requires a consistent effort from the officials that are working in public health," he said.

By his account, the work of restoring confidence sits with the people inside the public health system. He described it as a sustained effort over time.

The largest U.S. measles surge in more than three decades has come alongside falling immunization rates and rising vaccine hesitancy under Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Reuters reports. Several experts in that reporting said official messaging about MMR risks has made public concerns worse.

The connection between Kennedy and lower coverage rests on Reuters' reporting and on the views of those experts. Reuters describes the two trends as unfolding over the same stretch of time.

Kennedy's doubts about the shot predate his current role. Reuters reports that he has questioned the safety of the measles vaccine for years. The news agency adds that he has done so without scientific evidence.

The experts' criticism extends beyond Kennedy himself. They pointed to statements from both Kennedy and the White House about the risks of the MMR vaccine. In their assessment, that messaging worsened concerns the public already held.

Those concerns did not begin with the current administration. Trust in vaccination dropped during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, and the experts said federal messaging has added to that decline.

The CDC's official stance differs from the criticism the experts described. The agency says it supports measles vaccination.

The federal government has publicly pushed several states to loosen their school vaccine mandates, according to Reuters. It has also spent millions of dollars investigating vaccine safety.

These are two distinct lines of federal action. The mandate pressure targets the requirements that individual states set for children attending school. The safety spending directs federal money toward reexamining vaccines.

School vaccine mandates are set at the state level. That is why the federal push has taken the form of public pressure on states rather than a direct change to the rules.

Every measles case recorded in the U.S. over the past two years began as a virus imported from another country, according to Walter Orenstein, a professor emeritus at Emory University. He said Americans traveling abroad often carried the virus home.

In Orenstein's account, those imported infections did not stay contained. Travelers $TRV who returned with the virus went on to set off outbreaks in their local communities.

Orenstein said the U.S. needs to resume its support for global immunization efforts. He said that support was disrupted when the U.S. left the World Health Organization.

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) judged U.S. measles status by asking whether a single strain of the virus had circulated in the country for 12 months or longer. A senior Trump administration official, speaking anonymously, said the Utah outbreak, which began in June 2025, was key to that determination.

The test turns on how long one strain kept spreading, not on the size of any single outbreak. What matters is whether the same strain moved through the country without a break for a full year.

PAHO reviewed epidemiological and laboratory evidence supplied by the CDC to answer that question. Together, the two kinds of evidence let reviewers tie individual cases to a specific strain and place them on a timeline.

The week before the official described PAHO's letter, a U.S. independent advisory panel presented the CDC's measles status report to PAHO. The panel added its own assessment that the U.S. had likely lost elimination status.

Walter Orenstein, a professor emeritus at Emory University, served on that panel.

The panel's assessment and the official's account point in the same direction. PAHO's formal announcement was still expected when the official spoke.

To regain measles elimination status, the U.S. must show that transmission has stopped and has not been sustained for 12 months. It also needs a high-quality surveillance system that functions.

The two conditions are linked. Proving that no chain of spread has lasted a full year requires a system that can find and confirm cases. Without reliable detection, the first condition cannot be shown.

Jennifer Nuzzo, director of the Pandemic Center at Brown University, pointed to outbreaks that keep appearing in Pennsylvania, New York and Wisconsin. In her view, there is no clear evidence that national transmission has ended. She also said it is unlikely that every case is being counted.

Her two points bear on both requirements. Continuing outbreaks in three states work against the first condition. Cases that go uncounted point to a weakness in the second.

Two further public health tools are needed. The first is a stronger surveillance network that can identify the measles virus and test for it. The second is more epidemiological capacity. That means the ability to follow up on cases and break chains of transmission.

The two tools serve different stages of a response. Surveillance finds the virus. Epidemiological follow-up works to stop it from passing from one person to the next.

Dr. Ben Kasstan-Dabush, assistant professor of global health and development at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, said the U.S. needs to raise vaccination across all groups. His emphasis is on breadth, with coverage rising in every group rather than in a single population.

CDC Director Erica Schwartz, who has held the job for three months, told Reuters last week that the agency would not change its response if elimination status is lost. She made that comment before PAHO's expected formal announcement.

#5362. /C O R R E C T I O N - Finzly/

In the news release, Finzly Appoints Former Early Warning Services CEO Paul Finch to Its Board of Directors, issued 16-Nov-2026 by Finzly over PR Newswire, we are advised by the company that changes have been made. The complete, corrected release follows, with additional details at the end:

Finch helped launch Zelle and brings extensive experience scaling bank-led payments as Finzly accelerates adoption of BankOS.

CHARLOTTE, N.C., Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Finzly, a leader in modern banking technology, today announced the appointment of Paul Finch, former Chief Executive Officer of Early Warning Services and a key architect behind the launch of Zelle, to its Board of Directors.

Finch brings decades of experience helping financial institutions bring new services to market at scale. As a Finzly director, he will provide strategic guidance as the company expands adoption of BankOS, its modern bank operating system that enables banks to modernize payments and introduce new banking capabilities alongside their existing core systems.

As CEO of Early Warning Services from 2003 to 2019, Finch led the expansion of the bank-owned company's capabilities in payments, fraud prevention, and identity verification. Under his leadership, Early Warning worked with leading U.S. financial institutions to launch Zelle in 2017, making real-time payments available to millions of Americans through their banks.

"Paul has already helped transform how America moves money. Now, we have an opportunity to transform how America banks," said Booshan Rengachari, Founder and CEO of Finzly. "Paul understands what it takes to earn banks' trust, build industry-wide collaboration, and bring new services to market at scale. His experience will be invaluable as we bring BankOS to more financial institutions, helping them innovate faster and deliver next-generation banking experiences without being constrained by legacy technology."

Finzly is advancing its strategy to enable banks of all sizes to rapidly introduce new products, connect to emerging payment networks, seamlessly integrate acquired businesses, harness AI capabilities, and deliver differentiated financial experiences while maintaining control of their infrastructure and customer relationships.

"The financial services industry is entering a new era of transformation, and banks need the freedom to innovate without being held back by legacy infrastructure," said Paul Finch, incoming member of Finzly's Board of Directors. "Booshan and the Finzly team have built a compelling platform that addresses this challenge. BankOS allows banks to modernize progressively while preserving their existing investments and accelerating innovation. I'm excited to join the board and help Finzly scale its impact across the banking industry."

"Finzly has built a strong foundation for its next chapter of growth," said Shamit Mehta, a member of Finzly's Board of Directors and Partner at TZP Group. "Paul's experience in building and scaling one of America's most successful payment networks brings invaluable expertise and industry perspective to our Board. I believe the combination of Finzly's technology, entrepreneurial drive, and Paul's industry leadership positions the company to play an increasingly important role in shaping the future of banking."

Finzly is a banking technology company on a mission to modernize the financial infrastructure that powers banks and credit unions. Its flagship platform, BankOS, is an AI-native, API-first, event-driven bank operating system enabling financial institutions to progressively modernize legacy systems and rapidly introduce new banking capabilities.

Through its modular platform spanning payments, accounts, digital banking, foreign exchange, tokenized deposits, and agentic AI, Finzly enables financial institutions to innovate faster, operate more efficiently, and grow through mergers and acquisitions without technology becoming a barrier to their strategic ambitions.

Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, Finzly is helping shape the future of banking with secure, scalable, and interoperable infrastructure.

For more information, visit www.finzly.com.
